entries.content: I've been taking berberine for about 18 months now and my A1C dropped from 7.8 to 6.9. My doctor wanted to increase my metformin but I decided to try berberine first based on what I read in our group. The research on berberine is solid—it activates the same pathways as prescription medications. I take 500mg three times daily with meals and track my numbers religiously. For me, this has been a game changer and I avoided having to up my prescription dose.

Berberine is a compound found in several plants including goldenseal and barberry. Studies have shown it may help lower blood glucose levels through multiple mechanisms including improving insulin sensitivity. Common dosing in studies ranges from 900-1500mg daily divided into multiple doses. Side effects can include gastrointestinal discomfort, and it has known interactions with several medication classes.

In diabetes support communities, berberine is frequently discussed as a supplement that members have incorporated into their routines. Many community members report sharing their experiences of maintaining stable blood sugar readings after adding berberine, with some noting they've used it as an alternative when they wanted to explore options beyond increasing their prescription medications. The supplement has gained popularity partly because it's available over-the-counter and has been the subject of clinical studies examining its effects on glucose metabolism.

Meta-analysis from 2023 covering 28 trials found berberine reduced fasting blood glucose comparable to metformin in several head-to-head studies. Participants taking 1000-1500mg daily saw meaningful A1C reductions. The mechanism involves AMPK activation similar to pharmaceutical approaches. Many practitioners in integrative medicine circles consider it a reasonable first-line option for people looking to manage glucose levels through supplementation rather than increasing conventional medication doses.

Quick update on my numbers this month. Had my quarterly appointment and went over everything with my endo. She adjusted my dosing based on my CGM data from the past few weeks. I mentioned I'd been reading about supplements online and she said she's happy to review anything I'm curious about at our appointments. The back-and-forth is tedious sometimes but I appreciate having someone who knows my full history looking at the data.
